notes:
Spec asserts: the real session runs ONE uninterrupted working span for the whole prompt — bash tool call plus the terminal 'done' reply — settling to ready exactly once at the end, and NEVER entering waiting. The recipe drives one auto-executed bash call ('echo hello'). Copilot is launched with --allow-all, so no permission.requested is written and `waiting` — reachable ONLY via the parser's permission_requested event — is structurally unreachable; if a recording ever flips to waiting here the bash call tripped a gate (the sibling gated-tool scenario) and the launch flags must be tightened, not this spec.

BIRTH RE-ANCHORED 2026-08-03: the real session is born directly into `working`, not `ready`. Copilot creates its session-state directory at launch but writes events.jsonl only when the first prompt is sent, so at discovery the file ALREADY holds the open turn; since commit 3cde4f8d ("fix(detector): classify every new session against its own metrics, not just children") buildNewSessionState classifies that birth against its own metrics instead of hard-coding StateReady. The transient proc-<PID> row (scanner.go:347) is still born ready and is still the presession_birth anchor. The pre-fix spec asserted a ready birth for the real session followed by a separate ready→working; that shape was the bug the fix removed, so session_birth and turn_start are now one phase.

KNOWN_FAILING CLEARED 2026-08-03 by commit 8df11518 ("fix(copilot): stop flashing `ready` mid-turn on a continuation turn"): the parser now maps assistant.turn_start to a non-settling activity event, so a turn opened after a tool call no longer reads as idle. Re-recording 2026-08-03-17-51-25_irrlichd-0.5.9+e31aad0 passes 4/4: the transcript again shows assistant.turn_end(turn 0) at 15:51:46.406Z immediately followed by assistant.turn_start(turn 1) at 15:51:46.409Z with turn 1's assistant.message only 4.1 s later at 15:51:50.537Z, yet events.jsonl carries exactly ONE working→ready state_transition (17:51:52.83, decided_by_rule agent_done) and no ready→working rebound — the 122 ms mid-turn false `ready` is gone. HISTORICAL (recording 2026-08-03-12-35-04, 3/4, pre-fix): the working span was NOT uninterrupted. Copilot closes a turn after every tool call and opens the continuation turn 1 ms later — this transcript has assistant.turn_end(turn 0) at 10:35:25.112Z immediately followed by assistant.turn_start(turn 1) at 10:35:25.113Z, with turn 1's assistant.message only arriving 2.1 s later at 10:35:27.223Z. parser.go maps assistant.turn_end to turn_done (→ ready) but lets assistant.turn_start fall to the default Skip arm, whose comment justifies it as "the open bracket of a turn the user message already put into working" — true for the first turn, false for a continuation turn, which has no preceding user.message. The daemon therefore settled the session to `ready` at 12:35:27.247 while the model was still generating, and only recovered at 12:35:27.370 via "force ready→working on first activity", flashing ready for 122 ms mid-interaction. The flash lasted only 122 ms here because the tailer's read of turn 0's turn_end lagged ~2 s behind the write; its true duration is the continuation's think time, so a longer tool chain shows a multi-second false `ready`. The phases below deliberately assert the CORRECT behaviour (one settle, no ready→working rebound) and the turn_end invariant is what fails.

OBSERVATIONS: cost/tokens are asserted non-zero and ARE derivable from the staged transcript offline (assistant.message.outputTokens is Copilot's live token signal; gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4-5 are both priced in the committed replay capacity snapshot). Input tokens land only at session.shutdown, which this recipe does not reach, so the input half of the summary reads 0. model is NOT pinned: --model accepts only `auto` and the router resolves gpt-5-mini or claude-haiku-4.5 per session.
